newsitem.title: USA: Stephanopoulos unworried about White House probes.
newsitem.headline: Stephanopoulos unworried about White House probes.

text.p: Senior White House adviser George Stephanopoulos denied on Thursday that he was jumping ship to avoid potential trouble stemming from investigations into the White House by independent counsel Kenneth Starr.
Stephanopoulos announced this week that he was leaving the White House, after working with President Bill Clinton for five years, to teach politics at Columbia University in New York.
"I have no fear of the independent counsel," he said on NBC's "Today" show. "That has no play in my decision at all."

He said he was confident that Starr would be unable to build a case against Clinton. "The president will answer the questions, and they will evaporate just like everything else has," he said on ABC's "Good Morning America."
Stephanopoulos said having political strategist Dick Morris, who is more conservative than others in the White House, steer Clinton's campaign for re-election had been uncomfortable at times.
"What the president did was set up some creative tension in the White House," he said. "Even though that's sometimes uncomfortable for the staff, it was the right thing for him and the country."
He deflected criticism of the White House's handling of the barrage of questions that have been raised about Clinton, his wife Hillary, and White House officials.
"When subpoenas are coming in a mile a minute, you always can't get everything out in perfect form right away," Stephanopoulos said. "We did our best. But we didn't always do it perfectly."
